walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 4: Film Music — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 4: Film Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 4: Film Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: A piece six bars long.
It is the very first section.
It is the same as the chorus.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: A piece six bars long.
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).

mcqs.q: How many crotchets are in a semibreve?
options: A piece six bars long.
